core.text: Attacked dependency for the fresh builder: sustained 900 rpm until three successive five-second side-image spreads are at most 4 percent is treated as necessary for uniformity. Attack both the high-speed requirement and optical control of duration with independently selected speed and time.

Failed account: every successful bounded trial requires sustained 900 rpm and optical stability. The stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded final attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207: approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounded counterexample defeats universal necessity; it does not establish reliable lower-speed sufficiency or calibrated concentration uniformity.

Surviving valued outcome transferred to the fresh builder: three elevation samples meeting the at-most-4-percent normalized attenuation-spread proxy at second 120. One stipulated trial already meets it after 60 seconds of 300 rpm stirring. Repeat success and stirring-time savings are hypotheses; the preferred procedure has no supplied total duration.

Proposed attack: fresh rinsed vessel, 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, commanded 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, then no restart before sampling at second 120. Record five-second optical checks without control authority. Keep dye bottle, addition location, camera and references fixed; alternate depth-sampling order. Within six trials, report raw readings, durations and failures; use spill tray and stop if liquid escapes.

residue.text: Optical fluctuations, differing surface depressions and transient bright specks survive as unexplained evidence. Bubble entrainment and agitation-renewed optical disturbance remain hypotheses. Matched 900 rpm final-vial readings are absent; specks cannot establish bubble identity.

Fresh builder must retain uncertainty from sampling disturbance, unverified actual rpm, repeatability without calibration and limited replication. Examine sampling-order dependence and preserve all failures. No inference extends to other liquids, vessel sizes or continuous operation.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds reliably suffices for this bounded sample proxy; sustained 900 rpm and optical stability are dispensable.
tension.account_b: Rival hypothesis: the observed lower-speed success was exceptional or sampling-mediated; fixed lower-speed repeats generally leave depth gradients.
tension.prediction_a: Fresh fixed-duration repeats meet final-vial spread at most 4 percent despite possible side-image failures, without systematic sampling-order dependence.
tension.prediction_b: Matched repeats exceed 4 percent or depend systematically on sampling order. Such failures would challenge reliability, without proving 900 rpm necessary.
